description: Cosmic Roots is an interdisciplinary team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We combine technology, data science, and scientific curiosity to explore innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Our mission is to turn NASA Earth observation data into actionable insights that help farmers make smarter crop rotation decisions, improve soil health, and build climate-resilient agriculture.
summary:
Field Shift is an interactive web decision-support system that helps farmers and agricultural extension officers across all 64 districts of Bangladesh design climate-resilient, year-round crop rotations (Rabi -> Kharif-1 -> Kharif-2).

To address the challenge, we combined 20 years of daily NASA Earth observations—NASA POWER agroclimatology, SMAP root-zone soil moisture, GRACE/GRACE-FO groundwater anomalies, GPM IMERG rainfall, and MODIS/ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration—with a 64-district agricultural database covering 50 seasonal crop options (cereals, pulses, oilseeds, fibre, tubers, spices, and winter/summer vegetables). Using a Temporal Attention Bi-GRU and multi-head Reinforcement Learning (Actor-Critic) model, Field Shift compares a farmer's existing rotation against four tailored strategies: Balanced, Water Conservation, Soil Health, and High-Value Vegetable. Farmers can also lock preferred crops or exclude crops they do not want to grow. Every recommendation explains why it was chosen, cites NASA satellite evidence, quantifies 20-year weather profit ranges, and flags local agronomic risks.

This matters because intensive rice monocropping is depleting aquifers and soil nitrogen across Bangladesh. Field Shift turns satellite data into practical rotation choices that save water, restore soil fertility, and boost farm income.
details:
1. What Field Shift Does & How It Works

Field Shift is an interactive, bilingual (English and Bangla) web decision-support system that helps farmers and agricultural extension officers across all 64 districts of Bangladesh plan climate-resilient, year-round 3-season crop rotations: Rabi (Nov–Mar winter), Kharif-1 (Mar–Jun pre-monsoon), and Kharif-2 (Jul–Oct monsoon).

  • Simple Farmer Inputs: A farmer only needs to select their District, Irrigation Access (tubewell/canal vs. rainfed), and Primary Goal. Optionally, farmers can specify what they currently grow, lock in a preferred crop for a specific season, or click crops they do not want to grow.
    1. Balanced: Maximizes farm profit while reducing irrigation demand and protecting soil nitrogen.
    2. Water Conservation: Protects groundwater in aquifer-stressed zones (such as the High Barind Tract) by replacing water-heavy winter Boro rice with drought-hardy pulses or oilseeds.
    3. Soil Health: Rebuilds depleted soil nitrogen using legume fixation (Fabaceae) and alternates botanical families to break pest and disease cycles.
    4. High-Value Vegetable: Selects short-duration winter and summer vegetables weighted by each district's empirical Area-to-Production (AP Ratio) yield index.

2. Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Water & Aquifer Protection: Replacing irrigated winter Boro rice and pre-monsoon fallow with climate-matched pulse/vegetable rotations saves 500 to 960 mm of water per hectare per year, easing deep-tubewell drawdown where NASA GRACE groundwater percentiles fall below 30%.
  • Soil Fertility Restoration: Legume-integrated rotations convert a baseline nitrogen loss of -61 kg N/ha/yr into a net gain of +13 to +38 kg N/ha/yr, reducing synthetic urea fertilizer costs and shrinking bare-field erosion windows.
  • Higher & More Resilient Farm Income: Increases annual net returns from roughly 1,150–1,320 USD/ha under traditional rice monocropping to 1,800–4,100+ USD/ha (displayed to farmers in local BDT per bigha, ৳/বিঘা), alongside 20-year Monte Carlo profit ranges across Bad Years (10th percentile), Normal Years (Mean), and Good Years (90th percentile).
  • Transparent, Evidence-Backed Decisions: Every recommendation includes five explainability blocks: (1) Why it was suggested, (2) Supporting NASA satellite evidence, (3) Agronomic and soil benefits, (4) 20-year climate uncertainty & resolution gaps, and (5) Risks requiring local extension review.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Coding Languages: Python 3, TypeScript, JavaScript (ES2022+), SQL, HTML5, CSS3.
  • ML & AI Frameworks: PyTorch (nn.GRU, multi-head Actor-Critic, Temporal Attention, AdamW, cosine annealing), NumPy, Pandas, Google Gemini API (bilingual explanation engine with zero-hallucination structured safeguards).
  • Web Frontend: React 19, Vite, React Router v7 (stateless URL query architecture—no login required), custom SVG Bangladesh district geovisualization, bilingual (English/Bangla) interface with real-time NASA climate cards, 20-year uncertainty bands, and what-if climate scenario sliders (-25% Drought, +2.5°C Heatwave, +30% Wet Monsoon).
  • Backend & APIs: FastAPI (ASGI REST API), Uvicorn, Pydantic v2 (schema validation), HTTPX (async client), Pytest.
  • Databases & Data Storage: SQLite3 (field_shift_bangladesh.db) storing normalized data for 64 districts, 72 crops (50 annuals + 24 perennials), and agronomic soil/market parameters; local multi-decade disk cache for NASA daily time-series; OpenPyXL.
  • NASA Datasets & APIs: NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (2004–2024 daily weather: T2M, RH2M, PRECTOTCORR, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, etc.), NASA SMAP Level-4 Root-Zone Soil Moisture (SPL4SMGP), NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO Groundwater Storage Percentiles (GRACEDADM), NASA MODIS & ECOSTRESS Evapotranspiration (MOD16A2GF, ECO_L3T_JET), NASA Earthdata.
  • Hardware & Environment: Multi-core x86_64/ARM workstations with NVIDIA CUDA GPU acceleration for model training and simulation; Astral uv virtual environment manager; Node.js/npm.

4. How Our Project Is Creative

  • Sequential Rotation Physics Instead of Single-Season Prediction: Most crop tools predict one crop in isolation. Field Shift treats the 365-day year as a connected sequence where winter crop root depth, harvest timing, and nitrogen fixation directly shape pre-monsoon and monsoon outcomes.
  • Multi-Head Pareto Menu Instead of a "Black Box": Rather than dictating a single crop plan, our 4-head Actor-Critic architecture presents a transparent menu of trade-offs (money vs. water vs. soil vs. horticulture) so the farmer stays in control.
  • Temporal Attention Stress Pinpointing: Our Bi-GRU encoder computes attention weights across twelve 10-day windows within each 120-day season, showing farmers the exact 10-day window when heatwave or root-zone drought stress peaks.
  • Data-Driven District Baselines: Instead of assuming every farmer starts from the same baseline, Field Shift automatically infers each district's dominant irrigated and rainfed baseline rotation from cultivated area statistics (e.g., Boro -> Fallow -> T. Aman in Rajshahi vs. Onion -> Jute -> T. Aman in Faridpur), while letting farmers customize their own.

5. Agronomic, Social & Technical Factors Considered

  • Agronomic Realism: We separated 24 perennial fruit/orchard crops (such as mango, jackfruit, and coconut) from 50 seasonal annual crops so the model never suggests uprooting multi-year trees after 90 days, and corrected spreadsheet season labels against actual transplanting and growing months.
  • Farmer Accessibility: We converted metric outputs ($/ha) into local Bangladeshi units (BDT per bigha) and built a plain-language glossary translating satellite metrics (like GWETROOT and ETc) into everyday farming concepts.
  • Honest Satellite Boundaries: Because NASA SMAP (9 km), GRACE (25 km), and POWER (50 km) capture regional conditions rather than individual plot drainage, soil pH, or local cold-storage access, every recommendation explicitly lists local checks to review with Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) officers before planting.

[Project Repository](https://github.com/NHHimmel/field-shift-nasa-space-apps-2026)
